newsitem.title: USA: Fidelity Investments to lay off 200-250 employees.
newsitem.headline: Fidelity Investments to lay off 200-250 employees.

text.p: Fidelity Investments, the largest U.S. mutual fund company, said Wednesday it plans to lay off 200 to 250 employees as part of a "mid-year course correction."
Fidelity spokesman Thomas Eidson said Chief Operating Officer James Curvy, who assumed the post two months ago, has been meeting with the operations committee and reviewing the firm's business plan.

"What we do in the second quarter -- what most businesses do in the second quarter -- is review the business plan and see where we are," Eidson said. "These 200 to 250 layoffs, whether for performance or for efficiencies, are part of a mid-year course correction."
He said that since the beginning of the year, "we have put 900 new hires on the payrolls and we have 900 open job requisitions company-wide."
Fidelity had $511 billion in assets under management in April. It also operates a myriad of smaller businesses including real estate ventures and a taxi cab company.
Hiring is mainly going on in the institution and 401K departments, Eidson said.

Michael Lipper, head of Lipper Analystical Services Inc, said of the layoffs, "This is an isolated incident. We would expect Fidelity to be year-over-year stable or adding employees, but in different jobs. Fidelity is too dynmaic an organization to be shrinking."
The staff cuts come at time when many mutual fund companies are adding workers amid record cash inflows and a roaring stock market.
"We have been adding staff all year and have 100 positions open," said John Hancock funds spokeswoman Susan Bishop. "So far this year, we've hired 49 people and in 1996 we hired 252."
Over the past year, all of Fidelity's domestic diversified funds have trailed the strong gains in the Dow Jones Industrial Average and the Standard & Poor's 500-stock index.
The year-to-date gain of 19.27 percent in the S&P index has in part fueled the rush of assets into Vanguard Group's Index 500 Portfolio, which tracks the index.
Fidelity's lackluster performance has caused the fund company's share of new assets to weaken.
